title: Transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy: a prospective randomized comparative study between the two-step and the single-step techniques

indication: mild to moderate myopia or myopic astigmatism (Methods: PRK candidates with myopia and myopic astigmatism within the stated inclusion limits)

notes: Target: Methods state refractive correction in both groups was based on the Wellington nomogram to achieve postoperative emmetropia in all included eyes; target recorded as plano.

Method: Methods state manifest and cycloplegic refractions were recorded with the auto-keratorefractometer KR-8900 (Topcon) and that postoperative MRSE was measured with the same preoperative tool; the tables label the series MRSE (manifest refractive spherical equivalent). Recorded as objective (autorefraction) because the stated instrument is an autorefractor; cycloplegic refraction is not tabulated after surgery.
Roles: two transepithelial PRK techniques compared without an investigational agent; neither arm is declared experimental, so both groups are control.
Attrition: 108 eyes of 54 patients enrolled; two patients in each group were lost to follow-up and excluded (not outcome-defined); 50 eyes per group analysed.
Both eyes of each patient were treated with the same technique and both are included (fellow-eye correlation within groups).
Table 2 also tabulates UDVA, CDVA, manifest sphere and manifest cylinder at the same visits (not extracted; schema 1.0.0 has no such series).
Mitomycin C 0.02% was applied for 30 s after ablation in both groups; standard postoperative regimen in both groups.
